 Marcus Smart, Amen Thompson, Kevin Durant, Jabari Smith Jr. and Alperen Şengün will start Saturday’s game against the Thunder. 
 While Şengün is back in the lineup after missing Friday’s loss to the Mavericks, Fred VanVleet (knee) is out for injury management. Smart will slide into the starting point guard role, while Şengün’s return pushes Clint Capela to the bench. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Fred VanVleet 
 HOU 
 Guard

 Fred VanVleet (knee) is out for Saturday’s game against the Thunder. 
 VanVleet will sit with right knee injury management and it likely won’t be the last time he does so this season. With Reed Sheppard (back) also out, Marcus Smart should move into the starting lineup Saturday against the Thunder. 
 Alperen Şengün 
 HOU 
 Center 
 #28 
 Alperen Şengün (back) is off the injury report ahead of Saturday’s game against the Thunder. 
 Şengün is good to go after sitting out Friday’s game against the Mavericks with back soreness. He should be started in all formats. Clint Capela will head back to the bench after picking up a spot start Friday. 
 Marcus Smart 
 HOU 
 Guard 
 #36 
 Marcus Smart (forearm) is available for Friday’s game against the Mavericks. 
 Smart is good to go after missing Houston’s last three games. His return likely means fewer minutes for Bogdan Bogdanović, who played between 15 and 20 minutes in the three games Smart missed. 
 Alperen Şengün 
 HOU 
 Center 
 #28 
 Alperen Şengün (back soreness) will not play against the Mavericks on Friday. 
 Şengün will miss the second straight game with back soreness. With Steven Adams already out, they started Tari Eason and Jabari Smith Jr. together at the power forward and center spots in last game. It’s possible they do the same again given the Mavericks positional size. 
 Marcus Smart 
 HOU 
 Guard 
 #36 
 Rockets head coach Ime Udoka said that Marcus Smart (forearm) is likely to play in Friday’s game against the Mavericks. 
 Smart has missed Houston’s last three games with a forearm injury, giving Bogdan Bogdanović more playing time. Look for Bogie’s minutes to decrease if Smart is cleared to play. 
 Reed Sheppard 
 HOU 
 Guard 
 #15 
 Reed Sheppard (back) is out and Marcus Smart (forearm) is questionable for Friday’s matchup with the Mavericks. 
 Fortunately for Houston, Fred VanVleet isn’t listed on the injury report. FVV should handle the bulk of the backcourt minutes, and Bogdan Bogdanović should see a significant boost in playing time. 
 Alperen Şengün 
 HOU 
 Center 
 #28 
 Alperen Şengün (back) is questionable to play against the Mavericks on Friday. 
 Şengün missed Wednesday’s game against Milwaukee, and head coach Ime Udoka opted to start Tari Eason, with Jabari Smith Jr. playing the small-ball center role. Clint Capela played extra minutes off the bench as well. Şengün’s return would push Eason back to the bench.

 Guard 
 #36 
 Marcus Smart (forearm) has been ruled out against the Bucks on Wednesday. 
 Smart will miss a third straight game, though reports indicated that head coach Ime Udoka was “hopeful” that Smart would return for this game. His next opportunity to suit up will be in Dallas on Friday, while his absence will allow Bogdan Bogdanović to continue to take on extra minutes off the bench.

 Kingston Flemings was ejected from Saturday’s game against the Pelicans with 3:04 remaining in the fourth quarter. 
 Flemings was ejected after an altercation with New Orleans’ Bryce McGowens. After McGowens blocked Flemings’ layup attempt, the rookie guard threw an elbow at the face of the Pelicans’ wing while play headed in the opposite direction. Multiple players from both teams left their benches, but no one else was ejected because the Hawks had called a timeout. Flemings finished with 12 points, two rebounds, six assists, four steals and one three-pointer.

 Naz Reid recorded 14 points (4-of-12 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), five rebounds, two assists and one block in Saturday’s loss to the 76ers.
 Reid has been in a bit of a funk since Charlotte’s October 24 win over the Heat. Over his last four games, the Hornets’ forward has shot 35.1 percent from the field and 21.7 percent from beyond the arc while averaging 12.8 points per game. That’s not the production fantasy managers were hoping for, especially as the Hornets continue to play without Coby White and Kon Knueppel. Hopefully, Reid can turn things around next week, with the Hornets hosting the Pistons on Monday. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Grayson Allen 
 CHA 
 Guard

 Grayson Allen accounted for 27 points (9-of-12 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, three assists, one steal, one block and seven three-pointers in Saturday’s loss to the 76ers.
 After scoring 14 points on 4-of-18 shooting in Charlotte’s prior two games, Allen needed a night like Saturday. He shot a stellar 7-of-10 from beyond the arc, including 3-of-3 in an 11-point first quarter. The 27 points are a new season-high for Allen, who scored 20 or more in two of Charlotte’s first three games. He’ll have a higher fantasy ceiling until Coby White and Kon Knueppel are cleared to return from their injuries. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson
